name: broad_greenwood
notes: AddTwoWayBikeLane(broad_street, right): 10 ft two-way lane, 3 ft buffer. Spends 13.82 ft of this leg's 51.14 ft between kerbs, leaving two 11.00 ft travel lanes with the centreline shifted -0.73 ft toward the left kerb, and 15.32 ft spare against that kerb. The NJDOT alignment does not move; every station and crossing frame is measured from it as before. NOTE: NJDOT's Bicycle Compatible Roadways and Bikeways (1996) calls a two-way bike lane on one side of the roadway 'unacceptable'; that guidance predates separated bikeways and MUTCD 11th ed. 9E.06 now marks them, but the departure has to be argued, not assumed - see STANDARDS.md 4.
AddBikeLaneBollards(broad_street, right): flex-post delineators at 8 ft in the 3 ft buffer between the travel lane and the bike lane - the traffic side, which is the side that needs protecting.

AddTwoWayBikeLane(broad_street_1, left): 10 ft two-way lane, 3 ft buffer. Spends 13.82 ft of this leg's 51.07 ft between kerbs, leaving two 11.00 ft travel lanes with the centreline shifted -0.67 ft toward the right kerb, and 15.25 ft spare against that kerb. The NJDOT alignment does not move; every station and crossing frame is measured from it as before. NOTE: NJDOT's Bicycle Compatible Roadways and Bikeways (1996) calls a two-way bike lane on one side of the roadway 'unacceptable'; that guidance predates separated bikeways and MUTCD 11th ed. 9E.06 now marks them, but the departure has to be argued, not assumed - see STANDARDS.md 4.
AddBikeLaneBollards(broad_street_1, left): flex-post delineators at 8 ft in the 3 ft buffer between the travel lane and the bike lane - the traffic side, which is the side that needs protecting.

ExtendBikeLaneThroughJunction(broad_street right -> broad_street_1 left): the bike lane's green carried across the junction as a dotted lane extension - MUTCD 11th ed. 9E.03(07) Standard (extensions through intersections shall be dotted) and 9E.06(15) Guidance (extension markings should cross intersections AND driveways for a buffer-separated lane); NACTO Urban Bikeway Design Guide, bidirectional lanes continue through intersections as a crossbike.
